evidence: The 1986 dissertation on the regional market of Iraq and the Gulf and the 1997 book on regional trade in Iraq, Arabia and the Gulf pursue the same specific research. A Cambridge journal bibliography identifies the dissertation author as Hala Mundhir Fattah.

USP identifies Vera Lucia Amaral Ferlini as its economic historian and explicitly lists A Civilização do Açúcar, Terra, Trabalho e Poder, Modos de Governar and História Econômica among her books, connecting the full-name CAPES entry to this bibliography.

The USP faculty biography lists the books under Vera Lucia Amaral Ferlini and identifies her as a USP history professor; USP thesis records also identify her as supervisor. This connects the USP repository-advisor anchor to the book author.
Deakin’s Michael Finch research profile explicitly lists A Progressive Occupation? (2013), credited to Finch MPM, connecting the Deakin reviewer to Michael Paul Maxwell Finch.

The 2000 Fort Stockton dissertation is by Maria Eva Flores at Arizona State. Maria Bernardete Ramos Flores is the UFSC historian of Santa Catarina and Brazilian culture, with a PUC-SP doctorate in 1991 and the listed Brazilian books.

UFSC’s biography of Maria Bernardete Ramos Flores explicitly identifies her as author of Tecnologia e Estética do Racismo: Ciência e Arte na Política da Beleza (2007), an exact book match to the LC author.

The 2004 Esdras Minville study and 2008 dissertation both examine French-Canadian traditionalist intellectuals, specifically including Minville. The book publisher identifies its author as pursuing a history doctorate at Université Laval, where the 2008 thesis was completed.

The catalogue of O Pão Nosso de Cada Dia (Paka-Tatu, 2002), on bakery workers and labour law in Belém, names the author in full as Edilza Joana Oliveira Fontes. Her 1993 Unicamp thesis studied the same workers in 1940–1954.

Paulo Roberto Ribeiro Fontes’s books concern Brazilian industrial workers, Nitro Química and migration to São Paulo. Paulo Vitorino Fontes’s works concern Azorean fishing and homelessness, recognition theory, Honneth and Portuguese social policy: a distinct author and research career.

The full-name academic profile of Paulo Roberto Ribeiro Fontes lists Trabalhadores e Cidadãos and Um Nordeste em São Paulo, identifying the latter’s English publication in 2016. These connect the CAPES name to the LC author’s books.

The 1972 thesis Comtian Positivism in Bengal and the 1975 book Positivism in Bengal have the identical distinctive subtitle, A Case Study in the Transmission and Assimilation of an Ideology: a direct thesis-to-book connection.

The 1950 Harvard dissertation Honoring Commerce and Industry in 18th Century France is catalogued under Charles Alvin Foster. The 1960 book on the evangelical united front is by Charles I. Foster; the different middle names and unrelated research distinguish them.

Scholae Palatinae belongs to Richard Ira Frank’s research on the later Roman Empire. Guadalcanal, Downfall and MacArthur are by Richard B. Frank, a Pacific War historian born in 1947 who graduated from college in 1969, incompatible with a 1965 doctorate.

The publisher page for Ordering time, nationalising the past gives ORCID 0000-0002-7946-972X and explicitly identifies its coauthor Fábio Franzini as author of À sombra das palmeiras (2010), directly linking the ORCID and LC bibliographies.

The 2007 USP thesis and 2010 book have the same distinctive title and subtitle, À sombra das palmeiras: a Coleção Documentos Brasileiros e as transformações da historiografia nacional (1936–1959), a direct thesis-to-book match.
